tagline: A narrow creek road through farmland and former trading centers.
intro: Cedar Creek Road follows its namesake stream past farmsteads, hay meadows, pasture and forested hills. The creek runs northwest from its source near Flatwoods to the Little Kanawha River. West Virginia’s Department of Environmental Protection identifies most of the watershed as forested, chiefly with deciduous trees. Designated a West Virginia State Backway in June 1996, the road passes buildings and homes dating from the mid-nineteenth century. The 41.42-mile drive takes an hour and a half, with five miles of crushed rock and 22 miles of one-lane asphalt.

Cedarville and Exchange were the corridor’s commercial centers. Exchange, once called Millburn, took its later name from the frequent changes of ownership of its mill and other businesses. It was also a Coal and Coke Railway stop. In Cedarville, a different change survives in the school building: the building served as a school until 1968, then became apartments.

Travel southeast through the Cedar Creek valley, passing the state park before Cedarville and continuing toward Flatwoods near the creek’s source. Cedarville takes its name from the creek, which in turn was named for the cedar trees along its course. The park contains a restored one-room schoolhouse and a log cabin used for campground check-in. Exchange is another historic stop, but its main structures were destroyed by fire in 2023.

moments.title: Cedarville
moments.text: Cedarville’s former school rests on a raised basement built from locally quarried stone. Above that foundation, the 1923 building has a wooden frame, two stories and a T-shaped plan beneath a hipped roof. The exterior is finished in striated stucco. Classes continued until 1968; afterward, the building was converted to apartments. The school joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1994.
moments.notice: The former school’s stone basement supports a stucco-finished wooden building.

moments.title: Flatwoods
moments.text: Flatwoods was a railway junction before the 1952 incident that made its name nationally familiar. The West Virginia and Pittsburgh Railroad extended a branch through town in the late nineteenth century. The Baltimore and Ohio later took over the line, with Flatwoods midway along its Clarksburg–Richwood branch. The event known as the Flatwoods monster UFO incident took place on September 12, 1952.

moments.title: Exchange
moments.text: Exchange’s name came from businesses changing hands: the local mill and other enterprises had frequent changes of ownership. Previously called Millburn, the community became a stopping point on the Coal and Coke Railway. By 2019, the main street was blocked, although the surrounding area remained populated. On August 25, 2023, a fire spread from one building to both sides, destroying the main structures and smaller storage buildings.

practical: Cedarville: For RV access to Cedar Creek State Park, use only the US 33/County Route 17 junction in Gilmer County. (checked 2026-10-11)
Exchange: Exchange’s main street was blocked as of 2019. (checked 2026-10-11)
